text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Turkish plane crashes after exercises over the Aegean.
- Chairman of Cyprus Airways is to be appointed by the cabinet next Wednesday instead of today.
- The United States want a military dialogue to start between the two sides in Cyprus before directing efforts to the substance of the Cyprus issue.
CYPRUS MAIL
- World Bank report on the future of the unspoilt Akamas peninsula generates fierce debate in House of Representatives committee.
- Greek parachutists are dropped for the final phase of Nikiforos exercise.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Sigma-Severis and Hailisco brokerage firms join forces. New 11 percent market share gives Sigma the top three rank.
- Woolworth sales forecast for 1996 is CYP 40 million.
- Accession talks with the European Union are due to begin in January 1998.
HARAVGHI
- Political party consultations continue ahead of municipal elections in December.
- Workers at Larnaca hospital go on 24-hour warning strike over unfair recruitments.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Greece's defence doctrine with Cyprus has been upgraded, despite pressure from abroad.
- Two thousand foreign workers in the hotel industry will be leaving Cyprus in November when their work permits expire.
SIMERINI
- Turkish F-16 crashes in the Aegean.
- Britain's envoy on Cyprus, David Hannay, has contacts in Athens and Ankara to assess their political will to move forward on the Cyprus problem. He arrives in Cyprus on Sunday.
- Civil servants employed on contracts warn they will go on strike if the House of Representatives fails to pass legislation giving them permanent jobs.
